name: Code Review for Claude Code
description: A multi-agent code review service that analyzes GitHub pull requests and posts findings as inline comments. Uses a fleet of specialized agents to examine code changes for logic errors, security vulnerabilities, broken edge cases, and regressions. Can reject pull requests when critical issues are found.
community_quotes: Reviews are billed on token usage and generally average $15–25 per PR
On average, reviews take about 20 minutes to complete
For large PRs (>1000 lines), 84% of automated reviews find issues (7.5 on average)
Human developers reject fewer than 1% of issues found by Claude
Caught an innocuous-looking one-line change that would have broken authentication

name: Tarvos
description: A reference implementation of Relay Architecture for Claude Code that automatically spawns fresh agents before context reaches degradation point. Enables AI coding to run indefinitely by cascading new agents with minimal handoffs. Each session runs in isolated Git worktrees.
community_quotes: Relay Architecture is a new way to run AI coding agents - instead of one agent executing your entire plan until it degrades, you run a relay
LLMs degrade as context fills up - by phase 4 of your plan, half the context window is spent remembering what was already done
That's not autonomous development, that's babysitting
Open source, MIT. Works today, rough edges exist

name: Superset
description: A turbocharged multi-agent IDE that allows developers to run 10+ AI coding agents simultaneously on a single machine. Agents work in isolated worktrees for parallel development on features, bug fixes, and refactoring. Supports Claude Code, Codex CLI, and other agents.
community_quotes: Run an army of Claude Code, Codex, etc. on your machine
Turbocharged multi-agent terminal for parallel AI development
